notation_and_syntax.notes: Name reachability, supported API, semantic contract, language enforcement, and security authorization are kept distinct.

Reproduced all three exact output lines.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The snippet is a namespace/contract demonstration, not a measurement of package import time, ABI, compatibility, or long-term stability.

evidence: Enumerated advertised exports and separately identified technically reachable private/helper names.
Checked that equal API symbol sets do not imply equal per-symbol semantic contracts.
Traced facade functions from owned tuple boundary through private implementation without returning _Rule.
Checked any actual dependency edge outside the permitted relation is an architecture violation by definition.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The single-file form cannot demonstrate package privacy; the limitation is explicit and exercises require built-artifact evidence.

evidence: Reviewed empty/large export sets, wildcard collisions, deep imports, leaked provider types/errors, generated declarations, reflective/serialization paths, binary/source/behavior/data compatibility, and unsupported accidental consumers.

Reviewed circular/lazy imports, import failure/reentrancy/idempotence/offline behavior, optional dependencies, package artifact omissions, ambiguous aliases, facade fan-out/ownership, and clinical-calculation exposure.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real multi-language builds, ABI tools, consumer repositories, packaged distributions, and clinical evidence remain outside the executable example.

evidence: Checked intentional/owned exports, stable owned boundary types, inward dependency direction, bounded deterministic import, reconciliation of export/docs/runtime declarations, governed deep imports, reviewable deprecation, and measured surface/fan-out/import cost against exposition and answers.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter does not mistake naming/documentation conventions for enforcement or version numbers for compatibility proof.

evidence: Reviewed the finite export/evaluation trace line by line.
Reviewed graph and compatibility statements as definitions or obligations whose proof requires complete artifact/dependency evidence.
proof_review.notes: No privacy, complete dependency restriction, binary/semantic compatibility, production packaging, or clinical correctness proof is claimed.

evidence: Audited public, private, supported, stable, compatible, exact, prevent, enforce, prove, must, and conclusion language.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Claims are qualified by language, artifact, observation, policy, and evidence scope; medical suitability is explicitly denied.

evidence: Reproduced deterministic exports, boundary tuple, and evaluation outputs.
Built-package, cross-language compiler, API/ABI diff, import-cost, consumer-contract, migration, and clinical evidence remains prescribed future work.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production compatibility, external academic/practitioner review, security boundary, or clinical suitability is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter applies Facade to language namespaces and integrates effective API inventory, export mechanics, boundary types, dependency direction, import behavior, re-export ambiguity, deep imports, compatibility, artifact testing, and cohesion.

practitioner_review.notes: Guidance covers explicit exports, owned contracts/errors, architecture rules, clean import/configuration, canonical paths, API baselines, external distribution tests, consumer contracts, deprecation telemetry, automated rewrites, rollout, and rollback.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review starts with a graph/set boundary model, supplies a runnable explicit-export example, broadens through ten language and production cases, and includes five complete exercises spanning surface analysis, design, compatibility audits, migration, and high-stakes transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
